text:
A typical year has 365 days.

In the context of the provided text, which discusses the vast timescale of the universe's expansion over 13.8 billion years, a year serves as a human-scale unit of time. While the Big Bang theory operates on cosmological timescales measured in billions of years, the concept of a 365-day year is a terrestrial measurement derived from Earth's orbit around the Sun, offering a familiar temporal reference point against which such immense cosmic durations are often contextualized.
